disposition_reason: Table 1 gives lead, cadmium and aluminum in 75 raw milk samples from artisanal producers (per litre); Table 2 gives the same metals in laboratory-made cream, skim milk, butter, ghee, cheeses, whey and yogurt.

study.design: cross-sectional survey of raw milk plus a processing experiment
study.origin: artisanal producers in four districts of Alexandria; processing milk from the Faculty of Agriculture dairy farm, Alexandria University
study.market: raw milk as sold to the public by artisanal producers, Alexandria, Egypt
study.method: flame AAS (Varian AA240 FS with HG 3000 accessory) after HNO3/H2O2 wet digestion of 2 g
study.qa: reagent blanks subtracted; no CRM or recovery reported

controls.outcome: Metals concentrated in cheese: type A Pb 535.51 (+24.11%), Cd 40.11 (+20.74%); type B (salted) Pb 745.87 (+72.87%), Cd 51.99 (+56.50%), Al 71.58 (+40.96%); wheys lower (Pb about 218-221)
Yogurt Pb 418.42 (-3.02%), Cd 31.26 (-5.90%), Al 50.66 (-0.27%); essentially unchanged

unresolved: Table 2 header gives ug/kg but the abstract and text report the same values in ug/l; recorded as ug/kg per the table.
The processing milk (Pb 431.46 ug/kg) is far above the survey mean (45.06 ug/l) and came from a different source (university farm).
Abstract states yogurt values as 'reduction' 3.02% while describing concentration; Table 2 R% sign convention is reduction relative to raw milk.
Named traditional products (two cheeses and a ghee by-product) are given generic labels.
